A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same GEMeX research. Text, figures, tables, and supplementary material are readable and can be matched across renaming, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GEMeX evaluations of ten existing LVLMs and a fine-tuned baseline in Tables 5–6, alongside dataset analyses and qualitative cases.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of two LVLMs and a SLAKE-CXR transfer experiment in Tables 4–5 and 7.

M1.justification: The OpenBioLLM re-grounding, GPT-4o question generation, and question-type-aware LLaVA-Med fine-tuning procedures remain. Expanded quality-control and prompt descriptions do not establish a new method component; the question-content categories were already analyzed in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on the chest-X-ray portion of SLAKE, previously discussed only as related work. This extends coverage to another dataset within the existing modality and open/closed-ended tasks. GEMeX's core coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: DeepSeek-VL and Qwen-VL-Chat are added to both GEMeX performance comparisons in v2 Tables 4–5. All ten previously evaluated LVLMs and the fine-tuned baseline remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces zero-shot SLAKE-CXR testing on 505 open-ended and 235 closed-ended questions. Section 3.2 also changes the reported generation filter from excluding reports with fewer than two sentences to fewer than three. Unchanged dataset counts and retained scores do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a cross-dataset transferability analysis and newly reports annotation-review outcomes. Conversely, v1's split-by-split question-content analysis becomes a pooled summary, removing the direct comparison across splits. Existing qualitative cases and other distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed protocols, confidence intervals, or significance tests for model performance. The additional evaluations retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All retained model scores in v1 Tables 5–6 match v2 Tables 4–5. New rows report average AR-scores of 67.89 for DeepSeek-VL and 62.63 for Qwen-VL-Chat. New SLAKE results include open-ended AR-scores of 82.78 versus 73.31 for the fine-tuned versus original LLaVA-Med model. Annotation-review counts and pooled question-content statistics are newly reported; split-specific content results are removed.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs. The evaluation definitions and Hungarian matching description remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain: a large chest-X-ray benchmark with four question formats, textual and visual explanations, challenging existing LVLMs, and benefits from fine-tuning. The expanded model roster supplies additional evidence without redefining these contributions; the conclusion retains its meaning.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the small number of radiologist corrections as evidence of generated-data quality and the SLAKE results as evidence of transferable X-ray knowledge. The existing task-specificity limitations, shortcut-reasoning interpretation, and metric recommendations largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies dated GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini identifiers, a 50-sample generation-prompt check, radiologist-review details, and configurations for the added baselines. Its generation prompt explicitly requests content-category labels. Hardware, training time, optimizer, and other fine-tuning settings are retained but moved to the appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to DeepSeek-VL, ChatCAD+, and medical-hallucination evaluation, while removing several citations, including CXR-CLIP and region-guided report generation. Qwen-VL was already cited in v1. The central positioning around dataset scale and multimodal explainability remains stable.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting and condensation affect the abstract, introduction, related work, and construction explanation. A separate Statistics section incorporates former appendix analyses, while generation prompts, training details, and model configurations move into reorganized supplementary sections. This substantially restructures the narrative beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: Figure 2 and several captions are revised; performance tables gain comparator rows and a SLAKE table is added. Distribution figures and prompt tables are relocated or resized, and three split-specific content plots become one pooled plot. Most existing plot designs and qualitative-case displays remain intact.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through additional comparators and an external SLAKE-CXR transfer test absent from v1. Model-version and annotation-review disclosures improve transparency. These gains are limited to a narrow transfer setting, while the unexplained filtering-threshold revision and removal of split-specific content plots introduce small clarity and detail costs. Overall, the evidence supports a modest improvement.
